title: Attached: The New Science of Adult Attachment and How It Can Help You Find—and Keep—Love
author: Amir Levine
Rachel Heller
target_audience: Individuals interested in psychology and attachment theory
Couples aiming to improve relationship dynamics
Readers of self-help literature focused on love and attachment
core_themes: Adult attachment styles and their origins
How attachment style determines relationship behavior
Understanding oneself and partners to improve relationship outcomes
Recognizing and responding to needs in romantic partnerships
Practical adaptation of attachment science for better relationships
primary_purpose: To introduce readers to the science of adult attachment and provide practical tools to identify their own and others’ attachment styles, ultimately empowering individuals to build healthier and more satisfying romantic relationships.

structure_format.organization: Organized into sections explaining attachment theory, describing the three principal attachment styles (anxious, avoidant, secure), illustrative case studies, and actionable advice

key_concepts_lessons: There are three predominant adult attachment styles: anxious, avoidant, and secure.
Attachment styles form early in childhood but continue to influence adult romantic behavior.
Recognizing your attachment style can help you understand your needs and emotional responses in relationships.
Choosing a compatible partner and responding constructively to differences can strengthen relationships.
Communication and secure attachment behaviors create more stable, fulfilling partnerships.
Attachment science can be used to break negative relationship cycles and build intimacy.
notable_features: Popularizes complex attachment research for a general audience
Includes simple self-assessment tools to identify attachment styles
Uses vivid case histories for relatability
Actionable, tailored relationship strategies based on attachment science
cultural_historical_context: Published in 2010, 'Attached' brought decades of scientific research from developmental psychology into public consciousness, coinciding with increased mainstream interest in self-improvement, emotional intelligence, and understanding the science behind healthy romantic relationships.
reception_impact: Widely cited as a foundational self-help book on relationships and attachment
Credited with introducing attachment theory to millions of adult readers
Praised for making psychological science practical and easily digestible
Some criticism for oversimplifying or rigidly categorizing complex relationship dynamics
comparable_titles: Hold Me Tight by Dr. Sue Johnson
Attached at the Heart by Barbara Nicholson and Lysa Parker
The Five Love Languages by Gary Chapman
Wired for Love by Stan Tatkin
